answer: Whether agents forecast a gale, map a canyon, or survey a knoll, their marketplace can allocate governance votes in proportion to tokens locked in escrow, rather than one vote per account. Splitting 100 locked tokens among a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens for the full lock period, tying up capital that cannot be spent elsewhere.
